blocks.value: Support is a price area where a stock has previously found buying interest. When the price moves down towards this area, buyers may become more willing to buy, which can slow the decline or lead to a bounce. Support is a way of describing a possible area of demand on a chart.

Imagine This: Drop a basketball onto the floor. The floor stops it from falling further and the ball bounces back. A support area can look similar on a stock chart: the price reaches an area where buying interest has appeared before. Unlike a floor, however, support is not a physical barrier.

Support can form when investors believe a stock is becoming attractive at a particular price, or when buyers who missed an earlier opportunity decide to enter. Some existing investors may also buy more near a level where they previously saw demand. These decisions can increase buying interest around that area.

For example: Suppose a stock falls towards ₹500 on three different occasions and then moves higher each time. Traders may identify the area around ₹500 as support. It does not mean the price must rise whenever it reaches ₹500; it means buyers have shown interest there in the past.

Support is usually better understood as a zone rather than one exact number. A stock may turn around slightly above or below the price where it previously bounced. The market is made up of many orders, so reactions rarely follow a perfectly precise line.

If the price moves below a support area, the earlier buying interest may not be strong enough to hold it. Traders may then watch whether the price stays below the zone or moves back above it. A break below support can be important, but it should be understood in the context of the wider chart and market.

Support does not guarantee that a stock will stop falling. A company may face new problems, market conditions may change, or sellers may become more active. A support level is an observation from past price behaviour, not a promise.
When you identify support, mark a reasonable price area and observe how the stock behaves around it. Avoid treating one exact price as a guaranteed buying opportunity.

blocks.question: What is a support area?
choices: A price area where buyers have previously shown interest.
A price fixed permanently by the company.
The highest price a stock has ever reached.
The amount of money a broker holds.

blocks.question: Why might a stock pause or bounce near support?
choices: The exchange forces the price to rise.
The company announces a dividend every time.
Buying interest may increase around that area.
All sellers are prevented from placing orders.

blocks.question: A stock repeatedly falls towards ₹500 and then rises. What might ₹500 represent?
choices: Its guaranteed future price.
A possible support area.
Its market capitalization.
Its annual profit.

blocks.question: Why is support better viewed as a zone rather than an exact price?
choices: Every stock trades at only one price.
Support is set by the company.
The stock exchange publishes a fixed support price.
Buying and selling activity can cause the price to react around an area.

blocks.question: What does a break below support tell you?
choices: The earlier buying interest may not have been strong enough to hold the price.
The stock must rise immediately.
The company has stopped trading forever.
The price cannot move any lower.
